# Liberal Democrats 2024 Manifesto Summary

## Economy and Business
The manifesto proposes managing public finances to reduce national debt as a share of GDP while investing in infrastructure. Key measures include replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy, expanding the British Business Bank, and creating Lifelong Skills Grants of £5,000 for adult education. The party would reform capital gains tax, increase the Digital Services Tax to 6%, and introduce a 4% tax on FTSE-100 share buybacks. Employment reforms include creating a "dependent contractor" status for gig workers, higher minimum wage for zero-hour contracts, and expanded sick pay eligibility.

## Health and Social Care
The manifesto commits to 8,000 additional GPs to enable seven-day appointment guarantees, expanded NHS dentistry access, and mental health hubs in every community. Cancer treatment would have a 62-day guarantee from referral. Social care would include free personal care based on the Scottish model, a Carer's Minimum Wage (£2/hour above standard), and a cross-party commission on sustainable funding. Unpaid carers would receive increased Carer's Allowance and statutory respite breaks.

## Climate and Energy
Targets include net zero by 2045 and 90% renewable electricity by 2030. A ten-year home insulation programme would prioritise low-income households. The party would remove restrictions on solar and wind development, maintain the fracking ban, and invest in energy storage. Water companies would face a sewage tax, bonus bans until pollution ends, and transformation into public benefit companies.

## Housing and Planning
The manifesto targets 380,000 new homes annually, including 150,000 social homes, through ten new garden cities and reformed land compensation rules. Renters would receive three-year default tenancies and no-fault eviction bans. Leaseholds would be abolished. Local authorities could increase council tax on second homes by up to 500%.

## Education
Proposals include a mental health professional in every school, above-inflation funding increases, and free school meals for all children in poverty. Teacher recruitment would be supported through independent pay review and funded training. A standing commission would reform qualifications, and maintenance grants would be reinstated for disadvantaged university students.

## Immigration and Asylum
The manifesto would repeal the Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda scheme, establish a three-month asylum processing standard, and allow asylum seekers to work after three months. Work visa policy would transfer from the Home Office to relevant departments. Family visa income thresholds would be reversed, and the Youth Mobility Scheme expanded to age 35.

## Political Reform
Electoral changes include proportional representation via Single Transferable Vote for MPs and English councillors, votes at 16, and scrapping voter ID requirements. The Ministerial Code would become statutory, donation caps introduced, and House of Lords reformed with democratic mandate. A federal UK structure would include a written constitution.

## Defence and International
Defence spending would increase toward 2.5% of GDP with Army cuts reversed. The party supports NATO, nuclear deterrent maintenance, and closer European defence cooperation. EU relations would follow a four-stage roadmap toward Single Market membership. International development would return to 0.7% of national income with an independent department restored.
